maya (runtime): Heads up — nightly perf alert on release/1.9. p50 token latency for text-gen increased ~28% on seq_len=512 after PR #4321 (kernel-selection heuristic). Canaries started to show increased tail as well.

drew: On it, kicking off a bisect. CI logs point to a change in the selector around commit abc1234. Selector now prefers gemm_v2 path for medium batch sizes which seems suboptimal.

jonah: Also seeing KV cache churn in the profiler around the same time window — eviction_count up ~3x. Could be related (allocation path changed in that merge).

ci-bot: nightly-perf-release-1.9 failure: p50 72ms -> 92ms, p95 210ms -> 320ms. Regression detected for workloads: seq_len=256 and 512. Full report: https://ci.internal/redwood/nightly/189512

charlie (release): Hold the canary rollout. I will open a hotpatch branch and coordinate cherry-picks. Nobody should promote the current canary.

maya (runtime): Bisect result?

drew: Bisect pointed to commit 1d2f3abc (merge of quant/selector-heuristic). Minimal reproduction locally:
```
# run perf harness
python perf/run_workload.py --model gpt-small --seq_len 512 --batch 4 --kernel-trace
```
Trace shows selector choosing matmul_v2 with slow kernel kernel_time=85us vs matmul_v1=62us for this workload.

jonah: Here's the profiler snippet around the spike (abridged):
```
2026-03-16T03:12: profiler: kernel_select time=42ms
  matmul_v2: calls=120 time_avg=85us
  matmul_v1: calls=48 time_avg=62us
kv_cache: evictions=124 -> baseline 38
```

maya (runtime): Root cause: threshold sign got flipped when merging the quant branch, so priority rule 'prefer_v2_for_quant' is applied for non-quant workloads at mid sequence lengths. Patch ready to flip back and add tests.

charlie (release): Plan: create hotpatch branch, cherry-pick the fix, run regression-suite on staging, if green cut v1.9.1-hotfix and push to canary. I'll also gate the release pipeline.

charlie (release): Commands I'll run:
```
git checkout -b hotpatch/release-1-9/kernel-heuristic-fix
git cherry-pick 1d2f3abc
# (or cherry-pick PR commit 2a7f4e5 if we have the patch commit id)
bazel test //runtime:selector_test --test_output=errors
```

sre-oncall: I'll pause the release pipeline and pin canary traffic to the last known-good revision. Also starting a targeted perf job on the hotpatch branch: `/run perf-nightly --branch hotpatch/release-1-9 --workloads seq_len=256,512`.

maya (runtime): I pushed PR #4334 to master with the fix and added an explicit unit test for kernel_priority with seq_len > 256. Also prepared a small KV eviction tweak (PR #4335) because the profiler showed some correlated churn.

drew: I've reviewed #4334 and confirmed it reverts the sign flip and restores the former heuristic. Local perf runs look back to baseline.

charlie (release): We'll cherry-pick both #4334 and #4335 into hotpatch. Who can approve the cherry-picks? Need 1 approver to proceed.

drew: I can approve. Tagged @maya for final sign-off. :+1:

ci-bot: hotpatch builds queued: 3/3 unit tests passed, integration queued.

jonah: After applying cherry-picks on staging: p50 72ms -> 68ms (baseline 66ms), p95 210ms -> 220ms (baseline 200ms). Much closer; KV tweak reduced eviction churn by ~40%. Recommend we run a few more runs to stabilize p95.

sre-oncall: Perf jobs stable after 3 runs, no regression on memory. Rolling canary to hotpatch once release approves.

charlie (release): Cutting v1.9.1-hotfix candidate tomorrow morning if no further regressions. I'll freeze the release branch until we confirm.

maya (runtime): Thanks everyone. Action items: (1) cherry-pick #4334 & #4335 into hotpatch (charlie), (2) run regression-suite + perf runs (sre-oncall & jonah), (3) promote canary if green (charlie), (4) postmortem + release notes (maya). I'll follow up with a short postmortem template once this lands.

drew: Approved and ready to merge when CI is green.

ci-bot: hotpatch build 1895123701: all checks passed, integration perf queued.

maya (runtime): I'll close the loop after cut and post the postmortem skeleton in #postmortems. Thanks for the quick responses — great cross-team coordination. :heart:
